The route takes you through a series of striking contrasts. In Buenos Aires, you can explore La Boca and San Telmo, watch tango or opt for a trip to Tigre, a gaucho ranch or even a day in Montevideo. In El Calafate, the main stop is the Perito Moreno Glacier. After Iguazú, the route leads to Brazil’s northeastern coast, where you spend the final days among beaches, cliffs, tropical greenery and warm ocean waters.

## Trip highlights

### Buenos Aires

Argentina’s capital combines broad streets, European architecture and leafy parks with neighbourhoods that have a strong local character. The itinerary includes La Boca, San Telmo, Plaza Dorrego, Plaza de Mayo and Casa Rosada. In the evening, you’ll see a tango show with dinner, Argentine wine and traditional dishes.

### El Calafate and Perito Moreno

In Patagonia, the city gives way to a cold mountain landscape. In Los Glaciares National Park, you’ll see Perito Moreno, a glacier whose movement you can watch from the viewing walkways. Huge chunks of ice break away from the glacier face and fall into the water before your eyes.

### Iguazú Falls

On the Argentine side, you can walk the lower and upper circuits and get close to the Devil’s Throat. The Brazilian side offers a wide view of the falls, which comprise 275 cascades. Over two days, you can see them from very different viewpoints.

### Praia da Pipa

The final part of the trip is for relaxing by the ocean. Praia da Pipa grew from a small fishing village into a popular resort. There are white beaches, emerald waters, cliffs and lush vegetation, as well as windsurfing, diving, shops, cafés and restaurants.
